title: PRO-Seq
scope: Kwak 2013 PRO-seq body profiling workflow depicted by the Illumina PRO-seq schematic and the middle PRO-seq poster row: four separate single-biotin-NTP run-on routes, extracted/hydrolyzed RNA, three biotin-dependent enrichments, 3-prime adapter ligation, 5-prime end repair and adapter ligation, and reverse transcription/amplification to separate cDNA libraries. The distinct PRO-cap and 4sUDRB-seq poster rows and the standalone EDTA drawing are outside this unit. The broader all-four-NTP and mixed labeled/unlabeled options in the current card prose are not substituted for the assigned single-NTP schematic.

method_scopes.rationale: All recorded local operations apply to the four separately processed A/C/G/U preparations in the depicted Kwak 2013 implementation. The repeated blocks use branch-specific States and Operation instances; a common caption does not imply pooling. The retained interfaces are the run-on preparation, RNA hydrolysate, purified RNA, 3-prime-adapted RNA, its purified preparation, end-repaired RNA with both adapters, final bead-bound RNA, and amplified cDNA. The first two capture/recovery procedures remain composite purification blocks rather than extra isolated fractions. Biotin labels the nascent-RNA terminal region and selects it; the copied cDNA insert is the final reporter. The source describes base-pair-resolution localization of engaged polymerase through RNA-origin 3-prime ends, not an unbiased census of all polymerase states. The card describes failure to detect arrested or backtracked complexes; that limitation is secondary catalogue evidence. PRO-cap is explicitly a separate initiation-site workflow, not a retained branch of this target.
